findings.title: Use the already available exact-source batch reader in specification and planning roles
findings.classification_detail: Source-confirmed engineering opportunity; impact remains unmeasured.

source_locations.role: Specification role directs one element_get/decision_get per required record.
Planning role repeats the individual-read sequence.
Implementation already prefers the batch reader and defines both cursor layers and exact single-record fallback.
Existing reader validates requests, shares one loaded state, checks ordered-query/source identity and budgets the response.
Existing source test compares paginated public batches to exact individual portions and checks envelope budgets.
Existing source test checks read-only metadata, exact equivalence and the 20-request bound; its timing diagnostic excludes model time.

findings.current_execution_path: For an explicitly bound product task, specification and planning prepare context, exhaust selection continuations, and are directed to read each required element/decision individually. Implementation of that same task already prefers product_sources_get_batch. The batch reader has no purpose-specific restriction in the inspected function and delegates to the same exact element/decision readers.
existing_optimizations: Context preparation already selects required sources instead of unrelated product content.
Implementation already documents batch consumption; no new batching API is needed.
The batch implementation loads state once per request and retains request-local integrity verification, bounded responses and source-specific continuation identity.
Shared state guidance permits same-actor exact text reuse only with retained text and correct owner/version/portion identity; this recommendation does not add a cache.
findings.unnecessary_work_or_restriction: The specification/planning instructions steer agents toward separate exact-source calls even when a bounded group can use the existing read-only batch operation. This misses existing request-local reuse and can introduce avoidable tool round trips. The source confirms the instruction asymmetry, not the number of calls a real agent will choose.
findings.reproducible_scenario: In an isolated product-linked task fixture, prepare specification-purpose and planning-purpose context containing several short required elements and decisions. Keep the selected pins unchanged. Compare following the current role text with the implementation role's existing 1-20-request batch sequence. Fully reconstruct both output sets before comparing text and pins. No live task is needed.
findings.minimal_recommendation: Update only the Specification and Planning role paragraphs in the authoritative shared protocol to prefer product_sources_get_batch for bounded groups when advertised, with exact single-record fallbacks. Reuse the existing implementation cursor rules: outer continuations use the identical ordered request list; incomplete portions use each item's cursor; an outer complete page does not mean every source is complete. Generate matching host copies only in a separately authorized implementation task.
findings.expected_qualitative_effect: Fewer separate tool dispatches and less repeated request-local loading for short multi-record product context; unchanged source text volume and unchanged semantic obligations. Large records can still require several portions, so no blanket savings claim is made.
findings.confidence: High that the API and guidance asymmetry exist; moderate that this improves end-to-end authoring latency because model/tool scheduling and actual record sizes are unmeasured.

guarantees.correctness: Read every selected original and every continuation. Do not replace exact sources with selection summaries or hashes.
guarantees.compatibility: Keep existing single-record tools as fallback for older serving runtimes and targeted rereads; resolve callable tools dynamically.
guarantees.state: Read-only change; no scope, consent, decision or generation mutation and no broadened source selection.
guarantees.recovery: Retain query/context/source identities across outer and item continuations. On stale context or changed sources, use existing reopen/reconcile behavior rather than combining snapshots.
guarantees.security: Keep response limits, pin validation and untrusted-source handling. Do not persist a cross-operation or global cache.

findings.measurement_plan: Use the existing isolated product-context fixture and public tool connection with both specification and planning selections. Capture exact records/bytes, call count, response size, integrity-read diagnostics and total tool wall time separately from model time. Include mixed elements/decisions, a large partial item, Unicode, stale/reordered outer cursor and changed pins. Then run a bounded fresh-context authoring trial with equal scope and compare semantic coverage, not just dispatch count. Report only observed differences.
findings.validation_plan: Preserve exact per-record text and pins against individual reads; exhaust both cursor layers; reject 21 requests, foreign/mismatched pins and stale/reordered continuations. Extend instruction checks to ensure both authoring roles route to the existing batch capability without changing mandatory source coverage. Reuse existing product-context tests rather than add a parallel batching subsystem.
findings.rough_complexity: Small instruction change and focused tests; no runtime API or schema change expected.
dependencies: Existing product_sources_get_batch capability on the serving connection

findings.title: Check manifest eligibility before loading design-stage quality manuals on the no-op path
findings.classification_detail: Source-confirmed instruction-ordering opportunity; no runtime saving was measured.

source_locations.role: Verifier and unconditional quality-reference reads precede the manifest no-design-output stop.
The actual design operation, evidence and handoff remain conditional on eligibility.
Main planning already skips Penpot/design schemas when no outputs are declared.
Integration reference explicitly limits itself to confirmed UI design outputs.
Scenario-only reads and schema-conflict-only inspection must remain in force.
Bundle integrity validation already verifies quality resources independently of model disclosure.
Inspected design skill test covers explicit routing/dependency and size, not this early-stop ordering.

findings.current_execution_path: An explicit post-plan design invocation verifies the matching bundle, reads engineering-principles, test-discipline and YAML-routing references, requires the specification and plan bundle, then checks whether the confirmed manifest actually declares any root design output. Only then can it report not applicable. External Penpot guidance and schemas are already correctly deferred.
existing_optimizations: No design stage is required without manifest-declared design outputs.
Penpot guidance, design schemas and external skills are already gated; the finding does not claim those are eagerly loaded.
The integration contract has one routing owner and reads only affected shared entries/screens.
The mandatory bundle verifier checks resource bytes/digests and dependencies before operation.
findings.unnecessary_work_or_restriction: On a valid post-plan invocation whose confirmed manifest has no design outputs, the agent is told to load the engineering and test manuals even though it will only return not applicable. Those substantive design-stage quality instructions do not determine eligibility; mandatory state-access guidance does.
findings.reproducible_scenario: Use a read-only fixture with an Approved specification, confirmed manifest, an existing plan/todo/handoff and no project_artifacts design outputs. Invoke the design entry in a fresh context. The current instruction order requests the two quality manuals before the no-op. Compare a reordered entry that obtains the same confirmed eligibility result first. Also exercise UI active with no outputs, UI inactive, and contradictory declarations.
findings.minimal_recommendation: Keep the mandatory bundle verifier and workflow-state/YAML access rules first. Obtain confirmed manifest eligibility before disclosing engineering-principles and test-discipline. Return not applicable for no declared design outputs; load both quality manuals unchanged for eligible work. Preserve reconciliation rather than migration for contradictory/legacy declarations. Do not create a new eligibility API or weaken approved-spec/plan preconditions for actual design work.
findings.expected_qualitative_effect: Smaller context disclosure and fewer required source deliveries for a no-op invocation. Eligible design execution is unchanged. Benefit is limited because correct main-planning routing normally avoids this invocation entirely.
findings.confidence: High on current instruction order; low-to-moderate on practical frequency and total benefit. This is a low-priority refinement, not a design-path performance regression.

guarantees.correctness: Use confirmed current manifest state, not filesystem screen presence or user-provided assumed eligibility. Fully load both quality manuals before any eligible design work.
guarantees.compatibility: No artifact, schema, Penpot route or evidence contract change. Preserve the current not-applicable outcome and legacy reconciliation behavior.
guarantees.state: Read-only eligibility; no manifest migration, output creation, handoff mutation or remote write on the no-op path.
guarantees.recovery: Missing MCP, unconfirmed scope or contradictory declarations remain unresolved blockers; no direct YAML fallback. Resume must re-obtain current eligibility.
guarantees.security: Keep bundle verification, state-access rules, exact scope boundaries and scenario-only managed-state reads before the early stop. No external skill or Penpot call on the ineligible path.

findings.measurement_plan: In isolated fresh contexts, record disclosed source paths/bytes, tool calls and wall time for no-output, eligible and contradictory manifests. Separate existing-context reuse from cold reads. Verify that eligible-path disclosure and final quality outcomes are unchanged. Do not infer token or timing savings from line counts.
findings.validation_plan: Add a focused instruction-order/trace case: no-output fixture obtains scenario-confirmed eligibility and returns without quality-manual disclosure, Penpot/schema loads or writes; eligible fixture loads both manuals before any design operation. Contradictory declarations still return to specification. Existing verifier failure must still stop immediately.
findings.rough_complexity: Small canonical-entry reorder and one focused contract/trace check; no runtime implementation needed.
dependencies: Separate authorization for generated distributions and tests

no_finding_checks.area: Progressive disclosure and repeated source reads
no_finding_checks.result: Existing guidance already prohibits rereading supplied project instructions solely for context, gates each profile on confirmed scope, maps one reference per active profile, and limits execution to packet-linked definitions. No recommendation to bulk-load all profiles or introduce a global cache.

no_finding_checks.area: Approval cadence, stage ownership and reuse
no_finding_checks.result: Scope confirmation, behavioral completeness and task-specific technical agreement have distinct ownership/purpose, not interchangeable duplicate approvals. Specification has no separate final approval question. Technical proposals can group a small explicit set, discuss shared decisions once and reuse adequate historical agreement. Plan acceptance does not execute packets. No recommendation to collapse these boundaries.

no_finding_checks.area: Optional implementation reviews and commit gates
no_finding_checks.result: Implementation independently preserves required local validation, but code/security review and commit are not completion/next-packet gates. It executes one explicitly authorized packet, preserves dirty worktrees and stops. Mandatory specification completeness review is a different semantic stage and was not mislabeled optional.

no_finding_checks.area: Independent completeness review, batching and inherited results
no_finding_checks.result: Current review guidance already uses bounded groups up to 20, a single coordinator write owner, pending-item resume and separate final whole-specification semantic judgment. Corrections-only followups preserve provisional historical attribution, permit scope expansion and never treat hashes as semantic independence. No recommendation to remove complete original consumption, final consistency or freshness checks.

MCP structural/receipt checks do not replace the independent reviewer's cross-section judgment or implementation's scoped-diff comparison. Existing execution guidance waits for local tests and restored mutations, then performs each required completion check once for current inputs. No executed redundant validation loop was established. The interview's 'After MCP writes' format-check wording alone does not establish that a project-wide command actually runs after every mutation; no measured or source-certain per-write duplication is claimed.

One behavior specification, sole completion checklist and current-only handoff already avoid transcript duplication. Lite packets stay compact; extra profile artifacts and durable documentation are conditional. Recovery reuses valid evidence only for unchanged inputs, and returns changed behavior/architecture to its owner rather than replanning silently.

no_finding_checks.area: Design stage external routing and evidence ownership
no_finding_checks.result: Design is separately invoked only for manifest outputs; main planning does not invoke Penpot. The integration contract has one external routing owner, bounded brief/outputs, no auto-install, scoped reads and no silent propagation to other specifications. Local structural pass is distinguished from independently observed exports, restoration, render/accessibility evidence. These guarantees should remain.

145 raw SHA-256 comparisons of already-reviewed non-templated references matched. Three generated incremental entry files use the expected host-specific question tool, project-guidance name and advisory model, with Codex-only frontmatter differences explained by the inspected renderer. This is a bounded fidelity check, not full distribution validation or installed-runtime evidence.
